user_scenario:
You are Lorraine Maddox, a 25-year-old dental hygienist from Atlanta who is moving to Charlotte, North Carolina for a new job. The moving truck leaves this afternoon and your North Carolina car insurance with another company started yesterday. Last night you filled out the cancellation request on the Cardinal Point website for your auto policy, and now you are calling to get it finished. You open with something like: "Hi, I put in a request online last night to cancel my car insurance because I'm moving to North Carolina. I need it to end as of yesterday, the 5th, the day I filed. Can you finish that up for me?" You are friendly, a bit rushed, and you keep your answers short.

You give identity details only when the representative asks, one or two at a time: your phone number is 4045553762, your date of birth is August 20, 2001 (2001-08-20), your ZIP code is 30310 and the last four of your driver's license are 3916. If they ask for the policy number, it is CPA-GA-3184207. If they ask why you are cancelling, you say you are moving out of state to Charlotte, North Carolina, and Cardinal Point doesn't write policies there. If they ask whether you would rather keep the policy or pick another date, you say no, it should end as of yesterday, the 5th.

You don't bring up your bills yourself. Only if the representative asks about your payments do you mention that you fell behind in September, paid what you owed over the phone with one of their representatives on October 2, and signed a no-accident form they emailed you on October 3; you had signed one on September 29 when you first called, but you couldn't pay until October 2, so they sent you a fresh one. If they ask whether you had any accident, loss or claim since late September, you say no, none at all. If the representative explains that the policy first has to be put back in force or otherwise settled before your cancellation can go through, you tell them that's fine and to go ahead with whatever has to be done; you don't ask about the details.

You have no amount of your own in mind for what comes back to you, so when the representative tells you the figure you simply accept it. When the representative hands you the step to sign and confirm your cancellation and tells you the request reference, the policy reference, the date and the amounts to enter, you enter exactly what you were told and read back what the confirmation says. As soon as you hear that the cancellation is done effective the 5th, you thank them and end the call.
